niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t a single “best” connected-TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals (brand awareness vs direct response), budget, target market, creative needs, and whether you want programmatic or direct publisher buys.

If you tell me your objective, budget, geography and target audience I can recommend a short list. Until then, here’s a practical way to think about it and some top options to consider.

How to choose a CTV agency (key criteria)
- CTV experience and case studies: Look for proof of outcomes on campaigns like yours.
- Platform relationships: Direct deals or preferred partner status with Roku, Hulu, Samsung, Vizio, Tubi, etc.
- Programmatic expertise: Experience with DSPs (The Trade Desk, Google DV360, Xandr/MSFT, etc.) and private marketplace deals.
- Measurement & attribution: Third‑party measurement (Nielsen, iSpot, Samba TV), unified reporting across CTV and digital channels, holdback tests/attribution models.
- Creative capability: Ability to adapt or produce CTV creative (30s/15s, interactive overlays, dynamic creative).
- Data & targeting: Use of household, people-based, and predictive audience segments while respecting privacy rules.
- Transparency and fraud prevention: Clear fee structures, viewability/fraud safeguards and inventory verification.
- Media buying flexibility: Can they do national, local, or addressable linear buys as needed?

Types of partners
- Large holding-group media agencies — best for scale, premium publisher access, cross-channel planning and enterprise-level measurement:
  - GroupM (WPP) — large scale + strong programmatic/measurement integrations
  - Omnicom Media Group (OMD, PHD) — creative + media orchestration
  - Publicis Groupe (Starcom, Zenith, Spark Foundry)
  - Dentsu (Carat, iProspect)
  - IPG Mediabrands (UM, Initiative, Matterkind)
- Independent specialists — often more flexible, performance-focused or creative-first:
  - Horizon Media (large independent with strong CTV practice)
  - Tinuiti (performance marketing with growing CTV capabilities)
  - Smaller boutique CTV shops — good for specialized strategies and faster turnaround
- Tech/platform partners (not agencies but critical to CTV success):
  - DSPs: The Trade Desk, Google DV360, Xandr/MSFT
  - Measurement / analytics: Nielsen, iSpot, Samba TV, Innovid
  - Publisher/platform ad solutions: Roku OneView, Hulu, Samsung Ads, Magnite/FreeWheel (supply-side partners)

When to pick which
- National brand awareness with cross-channel measurement: Choose a major holding-group agency with a dedicated CTV practice.
- Performance/direct response and tight CPA/ROAS targets: Consider a performance agency or a boutique CTV specialist that uses programmatic DSPs and dynamic creative.
- Local or addressable campaigns: Look for agencies with local inventory relationships and addressable TV capabilities.
- Tight creative needs (interactive, measured ads): Favor agencies that partner with Innovid, creative studios, and have in-house CTV creative experience.

Red flags
- No case studies or relevant experience
- Inability to show inventory sources or measurement partners
- Opaque fees or lack of reporting detail
- No programmatic expertise when programmatic buys are part of your plan

If you want a tailored shortlist, tell me:
- Goal (brand awareness, site visits, conversions, foot traffic)
- Budget range
- Geography (US vs international, national vs local)
- Timeline and whether you need creative production

I’ll recommend 3–5 agencies/platforms matched to your needs.
